relations.myth: Hera rears and settles the lion at Nemea
relations.note: Hera rears the lion and installs it as a calamity to humanity.

relations.myth: Hera nurtures the lion near Nemean Zeus
relations.note: Hera nurtures the deep-voiced, sheep-killing lion in Nemean Zeus’ country.

relations.myth: Hera orders the lion’s lunar production
relations.note: Hera commands Selene to produce, release, or cast down the lion.

relations.myth: Hera places the lion among the stars
relations.note: Hera places the slain lion among the stars as Leo.

relations.myth: Selene produces or casts forth the lion
relations.note: Selene bears, releases, or casts down the lion at Hera’s command.

relations.myth: Selene nourishes the lion in its cave
relations.note: Selene nourishes the invulnerable lion inside its two-mouthed cave.
Orthrus sires the lion with an ambiguously identified female.
Chimera probably bears the lion after mating with Orthrus.
An alternative reading makes Echidna the lion’s mother by Orthrus.
Typhon is named as the lion’s father in a later genealogy.
The Sphinx is the lion’s full sibling under the probable Chimera reading.
A late mythographic notice calls the Hesperidean dragon the lion’s brother.
Heracles hunts and overpowers the weapon-resistant lion in close combat.

relations.myth: Heracles kills the lion at Nemea
relations.note: Heracles kills the lion; later accounts specify strangulation.

relations.myth: Heracles skins and wears the slain lion
relations.note: Heracles flays the corpse with its claws and wears its hide as armor.

relations.myth: The lion bites off Heracles’ finger
relations.note: A late variant says the lion bit off one of Heracles’ fingers.

relations.myth: Athena supports Heracles during the lion combat
relations.note: Athena observes or supports Heracles during the combat in Archaic and Classical art.
relations.source: Archaic vase paintings and Olympia metope

relations.myth: The slain lion becomes the constellation Leo
relations.note: Catasteristic tradition identifies the terrestrial Nemean Lion with Leo.

relations.myth: A serpent assists Heracles against the lion
relations.note: An earth-born serpent reportedly fights beside Heracles against the lion.
